_doc: The four self-enqueue chains reachable from a LiveViewTest trigger in the studio tree, each labelled with its HOP COUNT: the number of zero-delay self-messages the LiveView sends ITSELF between the handle_event the test triggers and the handle_info that writes to the store. Hop count is what decides how many barriers a test needs: `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render/1` is ONE `GenServer.call(pid, {:phoenix, :ping})` (deps/phoenix_live_view/lib/phoenix_live_view/channel.ex, `def ping/1`), which orders only against messages ALREADY in the mailbox when it arrives. A 1-hop chain's send fires INSIDE the GenServer.call the trigger is already blocking on, so it is in the mailbox before the next ping and ONE barrier drains it deterministically. A chain of 2+ hops enqueues its next hop while the LiveView handles the previous one, AFTER the ping has been answered, so one barrier is not a drain and only a settle loop (ping until message_queue_len is 0, twice) is sound.

CH-PAPEROP.terminus: api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live.ex:328/342 handle_info({:paper_op, ...}) -> Lifecycle.paper_op/2 -> Shared.paper_op/2 (store write). The handler issues no further self-enqueue.

CH-AUTOSAVE.terminus: api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live.ex:321 handle_info({:autosave_form, form}) -> Lifecycle.autosave_form/2 -> Shared.do_autosave/2 (store write). No further self-enqueue.

CH-CHAT.terminus: api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/chat_live.ex:1287 handle_info({:dispatch_send, text, queued?}) -> ensure_session + wire write + persist. No further self-enqueue.

enqueue_sites: HOP 2  api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live/handlers/lifecycle.ex:316  tree_codelist_change/2 -> send_update(PaperFieldBlock, tree_value: code), which is Phoenix.LiveView.Channel.send_update/3 -> send(pid, {:phoenix, :send_update, {ref, assigns}}) with pid == self()
CH-TREE.terminus: api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live.ex:328/342 handle_info({:paper_op, ...}) (store write) — four generations after the trigger.
